mainTopic: Leading the condemned person out to סקילה: saving him until the last moment, and the source that the בית הסקילה is outside three camps
overview: The משנה teaches that once the trial ends, the condemned person is led out to be stoned at a place outside the בית דין. Along the way, a man waving cloths and a rider on a horse can stop the procession if anyone finds a reason to acquit, even the condemned person himself, as long as his words have substance. The גמרא asks how this fits with a ברייתא that places the בית הסקילה outside the three camps. It answers that both are true: the stoning place is outside the three camps, and it must also be away from the court itself, so the court won't look like killers, or so the condemned person has time to be saved. A ברייתא then learns the three camps through a גזרה שוה from פרים הנשרפין. Those bulls are shown to go outside three camps from extra words in the פסוקים. The גמרא asks why we don't learn instead from שחוטי חוץ, which needs only one camp. After weighing the similarities, it says going outside to make the act proper is the decisive match. רב פפא gives another source taken straight from the story of the מקלל. The גמרא's defense of his proof continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: After the verdict, he is taken outside the court to be stoned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens: once the trial is finished, the condemned person is taken out to be stoned, and the בית הסקילה was outside the בית דין, based on the פסוק "הוצא את המקלל".
steps.simpleTranslation: When the trial is over, they take him out to stone him. The place of stoning was outside the court, as the פסוק says: "Take out the one who cursed."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins a new topic: what happens right after a person is sentenced to סקילה. He is led out to a stoning place outside the בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a location rule: the stoning does not happen inside the court. It brings a source from the case of the מקלל (the blasphemer), where the תורה says to take him out before stoning him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
The trial has ended (with a guilty verdict)
The place where the stoning is carried out
The one who cursed (the blasphemer in ויקרא 24)

phrases.english: Mishnah: Once the trial has ended
phrases.notes: He means the trial ended with a guilty verdict and a sentence of stoning.

phrases.english: they take him out to stone him

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: The place of stoning was outside the court
as it is said: "Take out the one who cursed"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:14

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִגְמַר הַדִּין מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְסוֹקְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new משנה about carrying out the death sentence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the verdict, the condemned person is led out to a stoning place located outside the בית דין, learned from "הוצא את המקלל".

steps.title: A signal system that can stop the execution
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a man at the court door with cloths and a rider on a horse who can race to stop the procession if anyone, even the condemned person himself, has a real argument for acquittal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One man stands at the court's entrance holding cloths, and a horse is far away but close enough for its rider to see him. If someone says, "I can argue in his favor," the man waves the cloths, and the horse runs and stops them. Even if the condemned man himself says, "I can argue in my own favor," they bring him back, even four or five times, as long as there is substance to what he says.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and describes how the בית דין keeps a way to stop the execution while the condemned person is being led out. If a new argument for זכות comes up, the procession is stopped and he is brought back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court does not stop looking for זכות once the verdict is given. Anyone can trigger the stop, and even the condemned person himself can, many times, but only if his claim has real substance, so he cannot just stall.

keyTerms.meaning: Cloths or scarves used as a signal flag
To present an argument in someone's favor, toward acquittal
Waves
They bring him back to the court
Real substance in his words

steps.whatToRemember: The בית דין keeps searching for a reason to acquit until the very last moment. Even the condemned person can stop the execution repeatedly, as long as his claim has substance.
steps.confusionAlert: The "four or five times" does not mean the condemned person can stop things endlessly with empty claims. The משנה limits it: only if there is מַמָּשׁ (substance) in his words.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עוֹמֵד עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: One man stands at the entrance of the court
with the cloths in his hand
and a horse is far away from him
but close enough that he can see him
If one says: "There is an argument to make in his favor"
phrases.notes: This is one of the judges speaking up.

phrases.english: that man waves the cloths
and the horse runs and stops them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people leading the condemned man out to be stoned.

phrases.english: And even if he himself says
"I have an argument to make in my own favor"
they bring him back
even four or five times
as long as there is substance to his words

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד עוֹמֵד עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין וְהַסּוּדָרִין בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, describing what happens while he is being led out to the place from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A signal system lets anyone with an argument for זכות stop the execution. Even the condemned person can be brought back many times, provided his claim has substance.

steps.title: Was the stoning place only just outside the court?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: it sounds like the stoning place was right outside the court, but a ברייתא says it was outside the three camps, much farther away.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Was the place of stoning just outside the court and no farther? But a ברייתא teaches: The place of stoning was outside the three camps!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the משנה says "outside the court," while a ברייתא says "outside the three camps." These seem to give different distances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Outside the court" sounds like a short distance, maybe just past the door. The ברייתא requires something much bigger, outside all three camps (outside the city). So the משנה's wording looks incomplete or even contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more? (no farther than that?)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
The three camps (שכינה, לויה, ישראל)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ וּבֵית הַסְּקִילָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין הֲוָה
phrases.english: Gemara: And was the place of stoning just outside the court
and no farther?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה חוּץ לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת
phrases.english: The place of stoning was outside the three camps
phrases.notes: These match the camps in the desert: the camp of the שכינה, the camp of the לויים, and the camp of ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הַסְּקִילָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין הֲוָה וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the location rule in step 1 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the בית הסקילה was "outside the court."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires the stoning place to be outside the three camps, a much greater distance, so "outside the court" seems too little.

steps.title: Both are true: even outside the camps, keep distance from the court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees with the ברייתא and explains the משנה adds a separate rule: if the court sat outside the three camps, the stoning place must still be away from it, so the court won't look like killers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is as you said. The reason the משנה says it this way is for this practical case: if the court went out and sat outside the three camps, we still set up the stoning place away from the court, so that the court should not look like a court of killers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is right: stoning must be outside the three camps. The משנה is teaching something extra: distance from the court itself, even when the court is already outside the camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources are not arguing; they teach two separate requirements. The ברייתא gives the distance from the city, and the משנה gives the distance from the court. That second rule matters when the court sits outside the camps, and the reason given here is so it does not look like the judges are killers.

keyTerms.meaning: As you said
The practical difference that comes out of this
So that it should not
Killers, murderers

phrases.english: Yes, it is as you said
And the reason it teaches it this way
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה, which said "outside the court."

phrases.english: the practical difference is
that if the court went out
and sat outside the three camps

phrases.aramaic: עָבְדִינַן בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: we set up the place of stoning away from the court

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא מִיתְחֲזֵי בֵּית דִּין רוֹצְחִין
phrases.english: so that the court should not look like a court of killers

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ. וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי הָכִי, נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by accepting the ברייתא and reframing what the משנה adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are correct; the משנה adds a separate case and requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's "outside the court" seemed to be the only distance required, clashing with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Stoning is always outside the three camps, and in addition it must be away from the court itself, even when the court sits outside the camps, so the court won't look like killers.

steps.title: A second reason: time for a chance to be saved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another reason for keeping the stoning place away from the court: so the condemned person has a chance for הצלה along the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the reason is so that he may have a chance to be saved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason for the same distance rule. The walk from the court to the stoning place gives time for someone to find an argument in his favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays the same; only the reason changes. The first reason was about how the court looks, and this one is about the condemned person's benefit. It ties back to the משנה's signal system, which only works if there is time and distance before the stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another explanation
Being saved, rescue from the death sentence

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא requires the stoning place to be outside the three camps. The משנה adds that it must also be away from the court itself. The reason is either so the court won't look like killers, or so the condemned person has time to be saved.

phrases.english: Alternatively
so that he may have a chance to be saved

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתִיהְוֵי לֵיהּ הַצָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reason for the distance rule explained in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason for the same rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason for distancing the stoning place from the court is so the court won't look like killers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another possible reason is to give the condemned person time and opportunity to be saved.

steps.title: What is the source for 'outside three camps'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule that the stoning place is outside all three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the stoning was done outside the three camps. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 the ברייתא said the בית הסקילה was outside three camps, which is much farther than the court door. That is a big claim, so the גמרא wants to see where the תורה teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words? This is the standard way to ask for a source.
The three camps of the Jewish people in the desert.
The camp of the Divine Presence, around the משכן. Later this matches the בית המקדש.
The camp of the לוים. Later this matches the Temple Mount.
The camp of the rest of the people. Later this matches ירושלים.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Outside three camps' does not mean three separate places. The camps are like circles inside each other, so being outside the third one means being outside all of them.

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know the stoning place is outside all three camps, as the ברייתא in step 3 said?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having accepted the ברייתא's rule, the גמרא now asks for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the stoning place must be outside all three camps.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads 'outside the camp' as outside three camps
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the מקלל and says 'outside the camp' means outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Take out the one who cursed to outside the camp' means outside the three camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק about the מקלל and says it means outside all three camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'the camp,' in the singular. The ברייתא claims it means all three camps, but it has not proven this yet. The proof comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who cursed ה׳. The תורה commanded that he be stoned.
Outside the camp.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Take out the one who cursed to outside the camp"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:14

phrases.english: – outside the three camps.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'הוצא את המקלל אל מחוץ למחנה' is read as outside all three camps.

steps.title: Maybe it means outside just one camp
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own reading: maybe 'the camp' means only one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say outside three camps, or is it only outside one camp?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks itself a question. Since the פסוק says 'the camp' in the singular, maybe only one camp is meant. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the פסוק simply, the singular word 'camp' points to one camp. To say three camps, the ברייתא needs some outside proof.

keyTerms.meaning: You say. This opens the ברייתא's question against itself.
Or perhaps it is only... This brings up the other possible reading.
One camp.

phrases.english: You say outside the three camps,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only outside one camp?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר חוּץ לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A proof that 'the camp' means three camps and not just one.

steps.title: Learning from the burned bulls
steps.stepSummary: Using a גזרה שוה, the words 'outside the camp' by the מקלל and by פרים הנשרפין teach that the stoning, like the burning, is outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'outside the camp,' and by the burned bulls it says 'outside the camp.' Just as there it means outside three camps, so too here it means outside three camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its reading by comparing two places that use the same words, 'outside the camp.' The bulls that are burned go outside three camps, so the מקלל does too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזרה שוה: the same phrase in two places means the two cases share a rule. The proof depends on already knowing that the bulls are burned outside three camps, and that is the next thing the גמרא will check.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a rule from one case to another because the תורה uses the same words in both.
Bulls brought as חטאות whose bodies are burned outside the camp.
Just as there... so too here. This is how a comparison is stated.

phrases.english: It says here "outside the camp,"
and it says about the burned bulls "outside the camp."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:12

phrases.english: Just as there – outside the three camps,
so too here – outside the three camps.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה״, וְנֶאֱמַר בְּפָרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt raised in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the מקלל is taken outside three camps.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזרה שוה from the words 'outside the camp' by פרים הנשרפין, which are burned outside three camps.

steps.title: How do we know the bulls go outside three camps?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that פרים הנשרפין are burned outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by the bulls, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The proof in step 9 depends on the bulls being burned outside three camps, so the גמרא now asks how we know that. This sets up a second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the first case is solid. By the bulls the פסוק also says just 'the camp,' so the same question comes back there.

keyTerms.meaning: And there. Here it means the case of the burned bulls.
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the case that step 9 learned from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the burned bulls are taken outside three camps.

steps.title: The ברייתא says the bull goes outside three camps
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about taking out the bull and says it means outside three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'He shall take out the whole bull to outside the camp' means outside the three camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the burned bull as outside three camps. The proof is still to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of the three times 'outside the camp' appears by the bulls. It removes the bull from the first camp, and the ברייתא will now show where the other two camps come from.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull. Here it is the חטאת bull that is burned.
And he shall take out.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And he shall take out the whole bull
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:12, the bull that the כהן גדול brings.

phrases.english: to outside the camp"
– outside the three camps.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְהוֹצִיא אֶת כׇּל הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bull is taken outside three camps, as the ברייתא will prove.

steps.title: Again: maybe only one camp
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the bull perhaps goes outside only one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say outside three camps, or is it only outside one camp?
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the ברייתא asks whether 'the camp' could mean only one camp. This sets up the proof from the extra words in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as step 8, but now it is about the bulls. This time the ברייתא answers from extra words in the פסוקים about the bulls themselves, as the next steps show.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside only one camp.

phrases.english: You say outside the three camps,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only outside one camp?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר חוּץ לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַחֲנוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A proof that the bull goes outside three camps and not just one.

steps.title: The extra words by פר העדה add a second camp
steps.stepSummary: By פר העדה the תורה says 'outside the camp' even though it was not needed, so it adds a second camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה says 'to outside the camp' by פר העדה, it did not need to say it, since it already said 'and he shall burn it as he burned the first bull.' So it comes to give it a second camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that by פר העדה the words 'outside the camp' are extra. The extra words teach that the bull must also leave a second camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק already says to burn this bull just like the first one, so every rule of the first bull, including leaving the camp, is already included. The words 'outside the camp' are not needed for that, so they teach something new: one more camp.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought as a חטאת when the whole community sinned by mistake.
The פסוק did not need to say it. This means the words are extra.
A second camp, the camp of the לוים.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה״ בְּפַר הָעֵדָה,
phrases.english: When it says "to outside the camp" about the community's bull,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:21

phrases.english: which there is no need for the verse to say,
since it was already said

phrases.aramaic: ״וְשָׂרַף אֹתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂרַף אֵת הַפָּר הָרִאשׁוֹן״
phrases.english: "and he shall burn it as he burned the first bull"
phrases.notes: The 'first bull' is the כהן גדול's bull from step 11, which already went outside the camp.

phrases.english: – it comes to give it a second camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה״ בְּפַר הָעֵדָה, שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 12 by finding a second 'outside the camp.'
steps.raayaObject: That the bull must leave a second camp.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'אל מחוץ למחנה' by פר העדה, which were not needed because of 'כאשר שרף את הפר הראשון.'

steps.title: The extra words by the ashes add a third camp
steps.stepSummary: By the ashes the תורה says 'outside the camp' even though it was not needed, so it adds a third camp. This completes the three camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה says 'to outside the camp' by the ashes, it did not need to say it, since it already said 'on the place where the ashes are poured it shall be burned.' So it comes to give it a third camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds one more extra 'outside the camp,' this time in the פסוק about taking out the ashes. That adds the third camp and finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה already said the bull is burned at the ash pile, so we would know on our own that the ash pile is outside the camp. Saying 'outside the camp' again by the ashes is extra and teaches a third camp. Now the bulls are proven to go outside three camps, so the גזרה שוה of step 9 stands, and the stoning place is outside three camps too.

keyTerms.meaning: The ashes taken off the מזבח.
The place where the ashes are poured out.
A third camp, the camp of the rest of the people.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three 'outside the camp' phrases: the כהן גדול's bull, פר העדה, and the ashes. Together they teach that the burned bulls go outside three camps. Through the גזרה שוה, the stoning place is also outside all three camps.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אַל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה״ בְּדֶשֶׁן, שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The burned bulls go outside three camps, so through the גזרה שוה the stoning place is also outside three camps.

steps.title: Why not learn from offerings slaughtered outside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison to פרים הנשרפין. It suggests learning from שחוטי חוץ instead, where 'outside the camp' means only one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from offerings slaughtered outside the Temple! Just as there it means outside one camp, so too here it should mean outside one camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source it just gave. Maybe the stoning place should be learned from a different case that also says 'outside the camp'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'outside the camp' also appear by שחוטי חוץ, and there they mean just one camp. If we compare stoning to that case, the condemned man would only need to be taken outside one camp, not three. So the choice of which case to compare to changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
But let us learn (it) from
Just as there... so too here (a comparison formula)
Camp

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. פרים הנשרפין are bulls that are supposed to be burned outside, which is a מצוה. שחוטי חוץ are offerings slaughtered outside, which is an עבירה.

phrases.english: But let us learn it from offerings slaughtered outside?
phrases.notes: The source for this is ויקרא 17:3, where the תורה also says 'outside the camp'.

phrases.english: Just as there it means outside one camp,
so too here, outside one camp.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the stoning place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵילַף מִשְּׁחוּטֵי חוּץ

steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the stoning place from פרים הנשרפין (three camps)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another case with the same words, שחוטי חוץ, means only one camp. So the comparison could lead to one camp instead of three.

steps.title: It makes more sense to learn from the burned bulls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is more reasonable to compare stoning to פרים הנשרפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable that he should learn it from the bulls that are burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its original source. It says the burned bulls are the more sensible case to learn from, and it explains why in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two cases could both be the model, you choose the one that is more similar. This line only states the answer. The reasons follow right after.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense
Sin-offering bulls whose bodies are burned outside the camp
He should have learned it (from this case)

phrases.english: It is reasonable that from the bulls that are burned
he should learn it,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא, מִפָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by claiming פרים הנשרפין are the more fitting model.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the more similar case for the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought שחוטי חוץ is an equally good model, which would mean one camp.
steps.terutzMaskana: פרים הנשרפין are the better model, so stoning is outside three camps.

steps.title: Three ways stoning is like the burned bulls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists three ways stoning matches פרים הנשרפין: the word 'הוצא' (take out), taking it out makes the act proper, and it brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'take out to outside the camp', it makes the act fit, and it atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with three points of similarity between stoning and the burned bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, both use the word 'take out' (הוצא), which שחוטי חוץ does not. Second, going outside makes stoning and burning proper, while by שחוטי חוץ it makes the act forbidden. Third, both stoning and a sin-offering bring atonement (כפרה).

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because
Take out
Makes fit / proper
Atones

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא works. When two sources compete, it counts the points of similarity to decide which comparison is stronger.

phrases.english: Since it says 'take out'
phrases.notes: By the מקלל the פסוק says 'הוצא', and by the bulls it says 'והוציא'. It is the same word in both places.

phrases.english: to outside the camp,
it makes the act fit, and it atones.
phrases.notes: These are short labels for the second and third points of similarity.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן ״הוֹצֵא אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה״, מַכְשִׁיר וּמְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the claim made in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That stoning should be learned from פרים הנשרפין
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three similarities: the shared word הוצא, being outside makes the act proper, and both bring כפרה

steps.title: On the contrary, learn from offerings slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back and says שחוטי חוץ may be the better model. It sets up reasons that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn it from offerings slaughtered outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around with 'אדרבה'. This line is a setup: the reasons why שחוטי חוץ is the better match come right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three similarities just listed are not accepted as the final word. The גמרא now claims there are opposite points of similarity favoring שחוטי חוץ. So the question of which case to learn from comes up again, and step 20 settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary

phrases.english: On the contrary,
from offerings slaughtered outside he should learn it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִשְּׁחוּטֵי חוּץ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the previous step's conclusion and argues for the opposite comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that פרים הנשרפין are the more fitting model
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There are other similarities that point toward שחוטי חוץ. These are spelled out next.

steps.title: Four ways stoning matches slaughtering outside the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives four short reasons why stoning is more like שחוטי חוץ than like פרים הנשרפין: a person, a sin, a soul, and פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both cases it is a person, a sinner, punished with his soul, and פיגול does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lists the four reasons it promised in the last step. Each reason shows that stoning looks more like שחוטי חוץ than like פרים הנשרפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In stoning and in שחוטי חוץ a person is involved, he has sinned, and his life is at stake. פיגול does not apply to either one, but it does apply to the bulls. So on these points, שחוטי חוץ is the closer match.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (introduces the reasons)
A sinner, one who sinned
Soul, life (being punished with one's life)
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: These four words are short memory-tags, not full sentences. Each one is a separate point of similarity between stoning and שחוטי חוץ.

phrases.english: Since it is a person
phrases.notes: In stoning and in שחוטי חוץ we are dealing with a person. With the bulls, it is animals being taken out.

with the soul,
phrases.notes: Both pay with their lives: the מקלל by stoning, and the one who slaughters outside by כרת.

phrases.notes: פיגול does not apply in either of these cases, but it does apply to the bulls.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן אָדָם חוֹטֵא, בִּנְשָׁמָה, פִּיגּוּל

steps.title: Going out to make it proper is the stronger match
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא still prefers פרים הנשרפין, because there, just like stoning, going outside is what makes the act proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: Comparing one case where going out makes it proper to another case where going out makes it proper is better to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the four reasons. It says the ברייתא still chooses פרים הנשרפין because of one key point that outweighs them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For stoning and for the bulls, taking it outside is the correct way to do it. For שחוטי חוץ, doing it outside is what makes it forbidden. This match, going outside to make it proper, is treated as more important than the four other points.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes it proper, makes it fit
It is better to him, he prefers it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns three camps for stoning from פרים הנשרפין. Going outside makes both acts proper, and this beats the four similarities to שחוטי חוץ.

phrases.english: Making it proper from making it proper
phrases.notes: He means learning one case where going outside makes the act proper from another case just like it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing the similarities: one key similarity outweighs several smaller ones
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four shared features make שחוטי חוץ the better model, so stoning needs only one camp.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going outside to make the act proper is the decisive match, so we learn from פרים הנשרפין and get three camps.

steps.title: רב פפא learns the camps straight from the מקלל story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says משה sat in the Levite camp, so the first 'outside the camp' means outside the Levite camp and the second means outside the Israelite camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Where was משה sitting? In the Levite camp. The תורה told him, 'Take out the one who cursed to outside the camp,' meaning outside the Levite camp. Then, 'And they took out the one who cursed to outside the camp,' meaning outside the Israelite camp.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new way to learn where stoning happens, without comparing to any other case. He reads the two פסוקים about the מקלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was in the Levite camp, so the command 'take him out of the camp' means out of the Levite camp. The later פסוק, which says they took him out, adds a second step: out of the Israelite camp. So the תורה itself shows the person went out past both camps.

keyTerms.meaning: The Levite camp
The Israelite camp
The one who cursed (cursed ה׳'s name)
The Merciful One (ה׳, in the תורה)
Take out

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct proof from the story itself. It does not depend on the debate over which case to compare to.

steps.title: Maybe the second verse just says they obeyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the second פסוק is needed to tell us the people carried out the command, not to add a camp.

steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק has another job, telling us the command was carried out, then it cannot also teach a second camp. That would take away רב פפא's proof for leaving the Israelite camp.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)

steps.title: The obeying is written clearly elsewhere

steps.deeperAnalysis: If another phrase already tells us the command was done, then 'and they took him out' is not needed for that. So it can teach the extra step: outside the Israelite camp. The quote that proves this comes right after.
